new:
md5_match false means a written md5 was not among the PASS-graded md5s; the AAR reports it. The seats' duty is the check in the next paragraph.

ASK AAR SNAPSHOT CHECK (ASK 497). Who: the two graders of the AAR (W1 and W2 by default), never the coordinator. When: before each AAR is sent to the operator, in this order. (1) The coordinator inserts the AAR's rows. (2) The coordinator runs SELECT * FROM ask_aar_snapshots_check() and posts one line in the project chat: "ASK AAR rows written: <id> <row_md5>, ...", copying each row_md5 from the check's rows with check_code d. (3) Each grader first checks that the function's prosrc md5 equals its post-write readback, then runs SELECT * FROM ask_aar_snapshots_check() and reads the project chat with read_project_chat. The grader confirms, both ways, that every row in the table is on a coordinator line with the same md5, and that every id on those lines still exists with that md5. (4) Each grader posts the result on the AAR's Wall root. (5) Only then does the coordinator send the AAR. How to read the result: check_code d rows list each row and its md5 and are not findings. Any row with check_code a (a row whose written_by was not a session registered to seat 36 at or before its aar_at), b (the table, or one of its four triggers, missing or disabled), c (an audit row naming the table, its id sequence, its triggers or trigger functions after audit 38890; or audit row 38890 is not the ASK 493 build row; or a second ASK 497 build row exists) or e (an audit event trigger missing or disabled) is a finding, and so is any mismatch in step 3. A finding goes to the operator at once, plainly, before the AAR. The check sets TimeZone UTC itself, so row_md5 is the same from any session; compute no md5 by hand. Limit: checks a, b, c and e catch mistakes and careless posing; only the project-chat line holds against a seat that disables the triggers and the logging first, because no seat can post in the project chat.
